supporting_observations.claim: During the alert window, WS-TWEBER-01 made repeated connections to 10.51.20.30 on port 8080, the inventory's explicit web proxy. Examples occur at 13:40:27, 13:45:28, 13:50:38, 13:55:18, 13:59:44, 14:05:24, 14:06:10, and 14:10:13 UTC.

The repeated proxy connections are broadly consistent with the inventory's description of MediLedger checking for updates about every five minutes, but these records do not identify the application or requested destination, so they do not establish that MediLedger generated them.
The supplied records show the workstation connecting to the internal proxy on port 8080, but do not show the external HTTPS destination or directly establish the nature of the proxied traffic.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied proxy connection records lack request URLs, CONNECT targets, and proxy-side destination details; the records cited above only identify connections to 10.51.20.30:8080.
The supplied evidence does not associate the proxy connections with an originating process or executable.
The evidence does not include corresponding endpoint process-creation or application logs that could confirm whether MediLedger produced the repeated connections.
claims_not_established: Whether the repeated proxy connections were HTTPS tunnels, and what external host or service they reached.
Whether MediLedger or another process generated the connections.
Whether the proxied content was benign or malicious.
additional_evidence_needed: PROXY-PIN-01 access logs for WS-TWEBER-01 and the alert window, including requested host, URL or CONNECT target, response status, and transferred bytes.
Endpoint process/network telemetry for WS-TWEBER-01 during the alert window to attribute the proxy connections to an executable and user.
MediLedger updater logs and installed-software/version details to verify whether its update checks match the observed times and traffic.
unrelated_findings: Several internal hosts initiated TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443. The help-desk workstation's connection has TLS SNI WS-TWEBER-01.pinecrest.local; the other records show connections from WS-ARUIZ-01 and WS-RPATEL-01. These are inbound internal connections, not the alerted outbound proxy activity, and may warrant separate validation.
